title: Why Damon Chen started a YouTube channel after 8 years at one job and 4 years of solo bootstrapping
summary: Damon Chen shares his backstory: eight years at one job, quitting in 2020 to care for his child, and learning web dev that turned into side hustles and a full-time income. He explains his reasons for starting a YouTube channel: giving back, leaving memories, and having fun without monetization pressure.

principles.text: Side hustles are best started with the safety of a full-time job, so you can enjoy building without money pressure.
principles.quote: I still have my full-time job that's the reason probably the main reason that allowed me to fully enjoying doing the S hustling without worrying too much about making money

principles.text: Build hobby projects for fun; they can accidentally grow into a full-time business that out-earns your old job.
principles.quote: I accidentally fall in love with doing some sand hustling building some hobby projects and obviously four years later my hobbies become my fulltime and I can finally make living out of it

principles.text: Give back once you have your own stories, as earlier founders did for you.
principles.quote: four years ago when I just started and I've been helped by many OG Founders Founders that I admire like kland and Rosie from uh IND hackers

principles.text: Start new channels without growth or monetization pressure; if it isn't fun, it isn't worth the time.
principles.quote: I don't want to give myself you know especially at this moment any pressure in either growing the subscribers or doing some monetization

principles.text: Stop procrastinating on things you want to do; the best time to start is now.
principles.quote: there are only two best time to plan a tree uh the first one is 20 years ago and the second best is now

principles.text: Keep the team small but efficient and enjoy the work and life.
principles.quote: I have a small but very efficient team and for me I'm just enjoying my work in life at the moment
